domain: IoT device management & monitoring platform (ThingsBoard-style web console)
summary:
This application is the web console for an IoT platform that lets organizations onboard, monitor, and operate connected devices and assets at scale. Its users are tenant administrators who run the deployment, operators who watch and act on live data, and customers who are granted scoped visibility into the devices, assets, and dashboards relevant to them. The platform turns raw device telemetry into something people can see and act on: registering hardware, visualizing its data on live dashboards, being alerted when something goes wrong, sending commands back to devices, and giving the right people access to the right equipment through JWT-based authenticated sessions.

The application is organized around a handful of core entities — devices, assets, entity views, customers, and users — each of which can be created, configured, and assigned to a customer for controlled access. On top of these entities sits a dashboard and widget system: administrators build dashboards from a large library of widgets (charts, gauges, maps, tables, switches, knobs, alarm lists, hierarchy trees, date-range navigators) that bind to live telemetry or attributes via entity-alias resolution, arrange them in responsive/mobile-aware grid layouts with multiple states, and copy/paste widgets between dashboards. A visual rule-chain editor lets administrators wire processing nodes together (with copy/paste of rule nodes) to define how incoming device data is filtered and routed.

Beyond dashboards, the platform includes an alarm subsystem for operational oversight (filtering, selecting, and acting on alarms), an audit/event history subsystem for troubleshooting and compliance, a gateway/extension configuration layer for bridging external protocols (MQTT brokers, Modbus, OPC-UA, HTTP) into the platform, and import/export tooling — with built-in validation — for backing up or migrating dashboards, widgets, widget bundles, rule chains, and bulk entity data between tenants. Together these pieces give a single console to onboard, visualize, and operate an end-to-end IoT deployment.

useCases.title: Register and assign devices to customers
useCases.description: Onboard a new IoT device onto the platform and control which customer account can view and manage it.
steps: Administrator opens the device list and creates a new device via a registration dialog
Device credentials (access token) are generated via getDeviceCredentials and can be viewed or updated with saveDeviceCredentials
Administrator searches for a customer and selects the device(s) to assign
Selected devices are linked to the customer account via assignDeviceToCustomer, or made public via makeDevicePublic
Administrator can unassign devices from a customer (unassignDeviceFromCustomer) when access should be revoked

useCases.title: Register and assign assets to customers
useCases.description: Add a new asset (e.g., a facility or equipment group) to the platform and grant a customer visibility over it.
steps: Administrator creates a new asset via a registration dialog
Administrator searches for a customer while viewing the asset list
Selected asset(s) are assigned to the customer
Administrator can unassign assets from a customer later

useCases.title: Create and assign entity views to customers
useCases.description: Define a scoped view of an entity's attribute and timeseries keys over a fixed time range, and share it with a customer without exposing the full entity.
steps: Administrator creates a new entity view and picks the source device/asset
Administrator adds the specific attribute keys (addAttributeKey) and timeseries keys (addTimeseriesKey) the view should expose
Administrator sets a start and end time window (setStartTime/setEndTime) that bounds the view's data
Administrator searches for a customer and assigns the entity view to that customer
Administrator can unassign entity views from a customer

useCases.title: Build and operate a live IoT dashboard
useCases.description: Lay out, edit, and view a dashboard made of widgets arranged in a responsive, mobile-aware grid, with multiple states and the ability to copy/paste widgets.
steps: User opens a dashboard; its layout, states, and entity aliases are validated and loaded (validateAndUpdateDashboard, getStateLayoutsData)
Grid automatically adapts row/column sizing for mobile vs desktop viewports (checkIsMobileSize, detectRowSize, gridItemStyle)
User adds, edits, or removes widgets on the grid, or copies/pastes a widget between dashboards via the item buffer (copyWidget/pasteWidget)
Right-click context menus on the dashboard or a widget expose edit/export/remove actions (prepareDashboardContextMenu, prepareWidgetContextMenu)
Widgets subscribe to live telemetry and refresh in real time as the grid re-renders

useCases.title: Share and publish dashboards to customers
useCases.description: Control which customers can see a given dashboard, or publish it publicly for view without login.
steps: Administrator creates a dashboard and opens its assigned-customers manager
Administrator searches for and selects customers to grant access (addDashboardCustomers/updateDashboardCustomers)
Dashboard is assigned to (assignDashboardToCustomer) or removed from (removeDashboardCustomers/unassignDashboardFromCustomer) the chosen customers
Administrator can alternatively make the dashboard public (makeDashboardPublic), copy the shareable public link (getPublicDashboardLink), or revert it to private (makeDashboardPrivate)

useCases.title: Configure a widget's data sources and appearance
useCases.description: Bind a dashboard widget to specific devices/assets (resolved via entity aliases) and telemetry/attribute keys, and style how it displays that data.
steps: User opens the widget configuration panel while editing a dashboard
User adds a data source (addDatasource), choosing an entity, entity alias, or custom function; the alias is resolved to real entities behind the scenes (EntityService.resolveAlias)

User selects telemetry/attribute keys (onDataKeySelected) and sets colors/filters per key (showColorPicker, editDataKey), with sensible defaults pre-filled (getDefaultDatasource, initDefaultAlarmDataKeys)
User sets the widget's legend (onLegendConfigChange), time window (onTimewindowChange), header actions (onActionsChange), and alarm source (onAlarmSourceChange)
Configuration is validated and applied to the widget on the dashboard (updateValidity, onConfigChange)

useCases.title: Monitor live telemetry through visualization widgets
useCases.description: View real-time and historical sensor data through charts, gauges, maps, tables, and entity-hierarchy trees placed on a dashboard, with control over the time window being viewed.
steps: Widget subscribes to live data for its configured entities on load (WidgetComponent.createSubscription)
Incoming telemetry updates the chart/gauge/map/table/hierarchy tree in real time
User picks a historical or relative time range with the date-range navigator widget (onRangePicked, updateTimewindow)
User filters, sorts, paginates, or searches the displayed entities/records, or expands nodes in a hierarchy widget (updateSearchNodes)
User drills into an entity's details from the widget

useCases.title: Control a device remotely from a dashboard widget
useCases.description: Send a command (RPC) to a connected device directly from a dashboard control widget, such as a switch or knob.
steps: Widget subscribes to the device's current value and displays it live
Operator interacts with the control (toggles switch, turns knob)
Widget sends a one-way or two-way RPC request to update the device's value (DeviceService.sendOneWayRpcCommand/sendTwoWayRpcCommand)
Device confirms the update and the widget reflects the new state, or the widget surfaces an RPC error (clearRpcError)

useCases.title: Monitor and act on device/asset alarms
useCases.description: See alarms raised across monitored devices/assets, filter and select them, and trigger configured actions (such as acknowledge or clear) once addressed.
steps: Alarms table widget subscribes to and lists active alarms for the dashboard's entities (listenForData)
Operator filters alarms by search text (onSearchChanged) or reorders/paginates the list (onReorder, onPaginate)
Operator selects one or more alarms (toggleSelection/toggleAll)
Operator triggers a configured row/button action on the selected alarm(s) (onActionButtonClick, when actionEnabled)
Operator opens an alarm's details dialog to inspect field-level data for troubleshooting

useCases.title: Design and test a rule chain for IoT data processing
useCases.description: Build a visual pipeline of processing nodes connected by edges that route and transform incoming device data, reusing nodes via copy/paste and testing scripts before deploying.
steps: Administrator creates a new rule chain and opens the canvas
Administrator drags nodes onto the canvas and draws connectors between them to define the data path (connectorsOf, pathBetween, edgePath)
Administrator double-clicks a node to configure its settings, or right-clicks a node/edge for more actions (nodeDblClick, prepareRuleNodeContextMenu, prepareEdgeContextMenu)
Administrator copies rule nodes from one chain and pastes them into another (ItembufferService.copyRuleNodes/pasteRuleNodes)
Administrator tests a custom node script with sample input before saving, then saves the chain so it takes effect for incoming device messages

useCases.title: Configure a gateway's protocol connectors for device integration
useCases.description: Set up an IoT gateway device and configure connectors (MQTT, Modbus, OPC-UA, HTTP) — including broker credentials, data-point-to-attribute mappings, and RPC hooks — so external devices/protocols can feed data into the platform.
steps: Administrator creates a new gateway device (createDevice) and retrieves its access token/credentials (getAccessToken, getDeviceCredentials)
Administrator adds a connector/extension and chooses its protocol type (addExtension, openExtensionDialog)

For an MQTT connector, administrator configures broker connections and credentials (addBroker, pemCredentialsValid, changeCredentials) and maps incoming payload fields to attributes/telemetry (addMap, addAttribute, changeNameExpression)
Administrator configures request/RPC behavior (addConnectRequest, addAttributeRequest, addServerSideRpc) for two-way communication

Administrator saves the attribute configuration (saveAttributeConfig) and exports the generated gateway YAML/connector configuration files (generateYAMLConfigurationFile, generateConfigConnectorFiles) for deployment

useCases.title: View and edit entity attributes and relations
useCases.description: Inspect and update the scoped metadata (client/shared/server attributes) and directional links (relations) attached to a device, asset, or other entity.
steps: User opens an entity's attribute table, choosing an attribute scope (attributeScope), with filtering, sorting, and pagination (search, sortBy, onPaginate)
User adds a new attribute or edits an existing value, including raw JSON, and the table subscribes for live updates (getEntityAttributes, checkSubscription)
User selects and deletes one or more attributes no longer needed (isSelected/toggleSelected)
User views relations linking this entity to other entities, sets the relation direction (setDirection), and adds/edits/deletes relations as needed

useCases.title: Review audit logs and entity event history
useCases.description: Trace who did what on the platform and inspect the lifecycle/debug events raised by an entity, for troubleshooting and compliance.
steps: Administrator opens the audit log table for a tenant, customer, or entity
Administrator filters audit entries by search text or time window
Administrator scrolls to load more historical records
Administrator separately views an entity's event log, filtering by event type and time window

useCases.title: Manage customer accounts and platform users
useCases.description: Register customer organizations and manage the individual user accounts (tenant admins, customer users) that access the platform.
steps: Administrator registers a new customer account
Administrator browses and reviews the list of existing customers
Administrator views/edits a user's profile and role
Administrator generates and shares an account activation link for a new user

useCases.title: Import and export platform configurations
useCases.description: Back up, migrate, or bulk-load dashboards, widgets, widget bundles, rule chains, and entity data between tenants or environments, with validation applied before anything is imported.
steps: Administrator exports a dashboard, widget, widget bundle, or rule chain to a file (exportWidget, exportWidgetsBundle, exportRuleChain)
Administrator imports a previously exported configuration file; it is validated first and rejected if invalid (validateImportedWidget/validateImportedWidgetsBundle/validateImportedRuleChain)
For a widget bundle, each contained widget type is imported one after another (importNextWidgetType) and entity aliases in imported dashboards are re-mapped (prepareAliasesInfo)
Administrator opens the CSV import dialog and maps spreadsheet columns to entity attributes
Selected entities (devices/assets) are bulk-created from the CSV file

useCases.title: Author custom widgets and organize widget bundles
useCases.description: Write and live-preview custom widget code, save it as a reusable widget type, and group widgets into system-wide or tenant-specific bundles for easier reuse across dashboards.
steps: Administrator opens the widget editor, which renders a live preview in an iframe and provides a code editor with hotkeys and JS error reporting (initWidgetEditor, listenToPreviewFrame, initHotKeys, cleanupJsErrors)
Administrator saves the widget as a new or existing widget type (setWidgetType, widgetTypeLoaded)
Administrator creates a widgets bundle to group related widgets
Administrator browses system-provided or tenant-specific widget bundles when adding widgets to a dashboard (getSystemWidgetsBundles, getTenantWidgetsBundles)

useCases.title: Log in, log out, and navigate the console
useCases.description: Authenticate into the platform with a JWT session that is validated and silently refreshed, move between sections via the home menu, and end the session securely.
steps: User authenticates and the resulting JWT token is decoded and stored (setUserFromJwtToken, decodeToken)
On each request the token is checked for validity and transparently refreshed if near expiry (isJwtTokenValid, refreshJwtToken, resolveRefreshTokenQueue)
Home layout renders the navigation menu and workspace for the authenticated user
User navigates via breadcrumbs and the collapsible side menu, tracked by current state/URL
User opens their profile from the account menu
User logs out (UserService.logout), which clears the stored token (clearJwtToken/clearTokenData) and ends the session
